english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(t)=4t^{3}-15t^{2}+12t$, and let $g:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $g(x)=\max\{f(t):0\le t\le x\}$. Let $c$ be the point of $(0,\infty)$ at which $g$ is not differentiable. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0^{+}}\dfrac{g(c+h)-g(c-h)}{h}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(t)=4t^{3}-15t^{2}+12t$ द्वारा परिभाषित है तथा $g:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\max\{f(t):0\le t\le x\}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। माना कि $c$, $(0,\infty)$ का वह बिन्दु है जिस पर $g$ अवकलनीय नहीं है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0^{+}}\dfrac{g(c+h)-g(c-h)}{h}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f'(t)=12t^{2}-30t+12=6(2t-1)(t-2)$: $f$ rises on $\left[0,\dfrac12\right]$ to $f\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac{11}{4}$, falls to $f(2)=-4$, then rises
solution_full: $f'(t)=12t^{2}-30t+12=6(2t^{2}-5t+2)=6(2t-1)(t-2)$. So $f$ increases on $\left[0,\dfrac12\right]$, decreases on $\left[\dfrac12,2\right]$ and increases on $[2,\infty)$, with $f(0)=0$, $f\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac12-\dfrac{15}{4}+6=\dfrac{11}{4}$ and $f(2)=32-60+24=-4$.
The running maximum $g(x)$ equals $f(x)$ while $f$ is increasing from $0$, i.e. on $\left[0,\dfrac12\right]$. After that it stays at $\dfrac{11}{4}$ until $f$ climbs back to $\dfrac{11}{4}$.

$f(t)-\dfrac{11}{4}=4t^{3}-15t^{2}+12t-\dfrac{11}{4}$ has the double root $t=\dfrac12$ (local maximum), and dividing gives $\left(t-\dfrac12\right)^{2}(4t-11)$. So $f$ regains the value $\dfrac{11}{4}$ at $t=\dfrac{11}{4}$, and $g=f$ on $\left[\dfrac{11}{4},\infty\right)$ since $f$ is increasing there.
Hence $g(x)=f(x)$ for $0\le x\le\dfrac12$, $g(x)=\dfrac{11}{4}$ for $\dfrac12\le x\le\dfrac{11}{4}$, and $g(x)=f(x)$ for $x\ge\dfrac{11}{4}$.

Differentiability: at $x=\dfrac12$ both one-sided derivatives are $0$ (as $f'\left(\dfrac12\right)=0$), so $g$ is differentiable there. At $x=\dfrac{11}{4}$ the left derivative is $0$ and the right derivative is $f'\left(\dfrac{11}{4}\right)=6\left(\dfrac{11}{2}-1\right)\left(\dfrac{11}{4}-2\right)=6\cdot\dfrac{9}{2}\cdot\dfrac{3}{4}=\dfrac{81}{4}$. So $c=\dfrac{11}{4}$ is the only point of non-differentiability.
Write $\dfrac{g(c+h)-g(c-h)}{h}=\dfrac{g(c+h)-g(c)}{h}+\dfrac{g(c)-g(c-h)}{h}$. As $h\to0^{+}$ the first term tends to the right derivative $\dfrac{81}{4}$ and the second to the left derivative $0$.
originality_note: New: the running maximum of a cubic stays flat after the local maximum until the cubic regains that value; the corner there is measured by a symmetric difference quotient that adds the two one-sided derivatives (way 2). Closest known: JEE Main questions g(x) = max{f(t): 0 <= t <= x} asking the number of non-differentiable points. Different because: the regain point must be found from a double-root factorisation and the quantity asked is a limit that combines the two one-sided slopes.
